questions.question: With my income and my car payment, what is the most I could pay each month under Acme's DTI limit?
questions.answer: With your monthly income of $7,400 and your monthly debts of $900, the most you could pay each month under Acme's DTI limit is $2,430. This is based on a maximum debt-to-income ratio of 45% [Acme Underwriting Guide — Debt-to-Income §0].

questions.question: What is Acme's maximum LTV for a two-unit owner-occupied property?
questions.answer: For a two-unit owner-occupied property, Acme's maximum loan-to-value (LTV) is 85 percent [Acme Underwriting Guide — LTV Limits §1].

questions.question: If my rate lock expires and I extend it beyond the grace period, what does that cost?
questions.answer: If your rate lock expires and you extend it beyond the grace period, it will cost 0.125 points per seven days [Acme Product Sheet — Rate Lock Policy §1].

questions.question: My raise came through - I make 8,100 a month now. What is my income on file?
questions.answer: Your income on file is $8,100 per month.

questions.question: What income and monthly debts are on file for me?
questions.answer: Your monthly income is $8,100, and your monthly debts are $900.
